topics.label: Welcome and Introduction to Complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the complement system while setting expectations regarding its complexity and nomenclature.

topics.label: Complement Fundamentals, Nomenclature, and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles of the complement cascade, explaining its general organization, naming conventions, and the biochemical fulcrum of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways that converge to deposit C3b and trigger the complement cascade on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement targets and eliminates pathogens, including opsonization, recruitment-driven inflammation, and direct membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from causing collateral damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic or acquired deficiencies in individual complement components produce distinct clinical pathologies and disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the evolutionary strategies and mechanisms pathogens employ to evade complement destruction, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and provides framing for the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
